description: Per-entry module ceilings for the published packages, plus the frozen solidaria root-barrel inventory. Entries listed here have been narrowed off the root barrel and must stay narrow; the inventory holds the line for everything that has not been narrowed yet. A ceiling is raised only with the import that raised it named in the entry's `why`; see #565. The ceilings were re-measured once under #566 when the unit changed from dist chunks to source modules, and the numbers are not comparable across that change.
unit: Distinct source modules reachable from the source file an entry's `exports` target is emitted from, following static import/export specifiers, with workspace bare specifiers resolved through the imported package's own `exports` map and mapped back to `src/`. Type-only imports and build-time macro imports are not counted: neither reaches a consumer. Nothing here is tree-shaken, so a subpath barrel costs every module it re-exports — the number is what the entry's imports reach, and only an import can move it.

entries.why: 53 source modules, 47 of them solidaria. Three subpath barrels named in src/provider/index.tsx dominate: `@proyecto-viviana/solidaria/utils` (25 modules), `@proyecto-viviana/solidaria/i18n` (10) and `@proyecto-viviana/solidaria/overlays` (8). focus/FocusScope.tsx arrives through overlays/createOverlay.ts `import { isElementInChildOfActiveScope } from "../focus/FocusScope"` (#555, d0f095a1); upstream's useOverlay reads the same private helper out of @react-aria/focus, so it stays. utils/refs.ts and utils/owner.ts are the two files the Solid 2 port (#531) added, and utils/mergeProps.ts is solidaria's shim for the export Solid 2 dropped; all three are reached both through the barrel and directly, mergeProps.ts from `import { assignRef } from "./refs"` and `import { domAttrs } from "./domAttrs"`. The remainder is the provider's own 5 modules, solidaria's ssr and interactions entry points, and solid-stately's flags module, reached from solidaria/src/utils/dom.ts. Nothing here is tree-shaken: a subpath barrel costs every module it re-exports, which is why these numbers are roughly double the dist-chunk ceilings they replace. That is the unit doing its job — a barrel import is exactly the cost this guard exists to hold.
